A school mental-health programme and latent wellbeing classes (simulated)

programme.Rd

2,000 students, a school-based mental-health promotion programme (the treatment), five baseline confounders and eight binary wellbeing items measured six months later, which indicate a latent class (Flourishing, Moderate, Distressed). Designed for intervene_membership(): the effect of the programme on latent class membership. Because the data are simulated, the true effects are known (see Source).

Usage

programme

Format

A data frame with 2,000 rows and 15 columns:

id

Student id.

low_mood

Felt sad or down on most days (0/1).

worry

Worried a lot (0/1).

sleep

Trouble sleeping (0/1).

lonely

Often felt lonely (0/1).

hopeless

Felt hopeless about the future (0/1).

enjoy

Enjoyed everyday activities (0/1).

confident

Felt able to handle problems (0/1).

friends

Has someone to talk to (0/1).

programme

Took part in the programme (0/1): the treatment.

female

1 = girl (confounder).

age

Age in years, 13–16 (confounder).

low_ses

Low family socioeconomic status, 0/1 (confounder).

distress

Baseline psychological distress, z-score (confounder).

belonging

Baseline school belonging (confounder).

No values are missing.

Source

Simulated (no real person is described) by datasets/generate.jl of the Julia package LatentClassCausal.jl (seed Xoshiro(20261111)); codebook in its datasets/README.md. Participation is targeted at distressed, poorly connected students: P(programme = 1) = expit(-0.6 + 0.7 distress - 0.4 belonging + 0.3 low_ses

  • 0.2 female) (41 percent take part), i.e. confounding by indication. The follow-up class is a multinomial logit (Moderate = reference) with linear predictors Flourishing 0.3 + 0.7 programme - 0.6 distress + 0.4 belonging - 0.2 low_ses and Distressed -0.8 - 0.6 programme + 0.9 distress - 0.3 belonging + 0.3 female + 0.3 low_ses; the items depend on the class only (e.g. P(low_mood) .04, .35, .85; P(enjoy) .95, .65, .20). True effects (averaged over the sample's confounders): P(C(0) = k) = 0.440, 0.298, 0.262 and Delta = +0.179 (Flourishing), -0.059 (Moderate), -0.120 (Distressed). The naive comparison of participants with non-participants is close to zero. Licence: CC0 1.0 (public domain).

Examples

data(programme)
# participants were more distressed at baseline: confounding by indication
tapply(programme$distress, programme$programme, mean)
#>          0          1 
#> -0.2946344  0.4214927 
# \donttest{
# does the programme move students into the Flourishing class?
m <- latentmixtures::lca(programme, low_mood:friends, K = 3)
#> Starting Julia ...
intervene_membership(m, programme, treatment = programme,
           confounders = c(female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging))
#> ▸ Causal effect of a treatment on latent class membership
#>   AIPW, BCH pseudo-outcomes, 5-fold cross-fitting; N = 2000, K = 3
#>   Treatment:    programme
#>   Confounders:  female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging
#> 
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>            P(C¹=k)  P(C⁰=k)       Δ     SE            95% CI      p
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Class 1    0.626    0.430   0.196  0.031    [0.136, 0.256]  <.001
#>   Class 2    0.238    0.293  −0.055  0.036   [−0.127, 0.016]   .129
#>   Class 3    0.136    0.277  −0.141  0.022  [−0.183, −0.099]  <.001
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>   Δ = P(C¹=k) − P(C⁰=k); SE from the influence function incl. the measurement model.
#>   Diagnostics: entropy = 0.666, propensity range [0.019, 0.923]
# true effects: +0.18 Flourishing, -0.06 Moderate, -0.12 Distressed
# }
